newsitem.title: UK: European vegetable oil prices end little changed.
newsitem.headline: European vegetable oil prices end little changed.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices finished little changed on Thursday in quiet trading ahead of Malaysian export data expected on Friday.
European traders were awaiting the data from Malaysian cargo surveyors Caleb Brett and SGS with interest following talk in Malaysia earlier in the day of higher than expected exports for January.
"There was talk that exports could be as high as 560,000 tonnes during January but that does not seem possible," said a trader.

Traders said based on the SGS estimate of 401,932 tonnes of palm oil exports during January 1-25 the most they would expect would be in the region of 490,000-495,000 tonnes for all January, including lauric oils. "In the six days between the last SGS figures and the end of the month I would estimate that around 14,400 tonnes of palm oil has been pumped at the main ports, and that means all the pumps working flat out 24 hours a day," said one trader. "However, there are private ports with faster pumps, but I still don't think the figure will be anywhere near 560,000 tonnes," the trader added.

There was also talk that Indonesia was in the Malaysian market on Thursday but traders said there was no evidence of Indonesia in the physical market although they were probably in the futures market.
"The Indonesians are big speculators in futures but there is nothing to suggest they have been any more active today than any other day," said a Singapore based trader.
Traders in Europe see the weather in Brazil as the most important factor in the market at the moment.

"If the Brazilian soybean crop is good it's going to give the palm boys something to think about, because unless people really can't use any thing another than palm oil in their blends they are going to turn to the cheaper soft oils," one said.
At the close of business crude palm oil was $2.50 to $5 higher after Jan traded at $577.50 and $580, Feb at $572.50 and $575 and Feb/Mar at $570 and $572.50 a tonne cif.
Palm products closed $2.50 to $5 higher with no further business reported.
Coconut oil was $2.50 to $7.50 up at the close after Jan/Feb traded at $782.50 and $785, Feb/Mar at $770 and Mar/Apr at $762.50 a tonne cif in outright business.
Dec/Jan coconut oil also traded in a switch with Jan/Feb at a $2.50 spread while Jan/Feb switched with Mar/Apr with a $20 spread.
Palmkernel oil closed $2.50 to $5 lower and tradeless.
In a tradeless soft oil sector Dutch soy oil closed 0.50 guilders down and rape oil one to 0.75 guilders lower.
